tells.1: Forced casual asides ('and honestly, that's the fun part', 'your opinion will actually count') added to sound conversational, on top of bolded label headers ('The job:', 'Who we want:').
tells.2: Very even, polished cadence with stacked triads ('real days off, nights that actually end, and a schedule you can plan a life around'), though nothing glaring.
tells.3: The 'Day to day,' opener and the uniformly smooth paragraph rhythm feel slightly templated.
tells.4: none. The all-caps, run-on sentences, missing spaces after commas, and 'PREFERRABLY' typo are clearly human, though unskilled.
tells.5: Bolded template section headers ('What you'll do:', 'What we're after:', 'Pay:') in an otherwise prose post, a common AI job-post structure.
tells.6: Minimal. A slightly tidy colon construction ('full time and hands-on: you'll be...'), but it reads naturally.

reason: Version 6 keeps the voice and all the concrete details while cutting redundancy, and it avoids both template headers and manufactured casualness. Version 4 is unmistakably human but too sloppy and shouty to be credible for recruiting a sous chef.
